What performance, presentation, and production craft means here: Musical structure is the pattern of repetition, contrast, layering, and return that makes events relate across time. How the relationship changes the result: A repeated idea creates recognition; contrast changes expectation; return lets the listener compare what changed. Notation or an event map preserves those decisions for checking. Choice and tradeoff: More layers can enrich texture but hide a main idea. More repetition can create coherence but become predictable without meaningful variation. ATTACHED MANUEL ACADEMY LEARNER RESOURCE

Resource ID: ma-resource:ma-g10-arts-and-music-u04-l07

Lesson focus: performance, presentation, and production craft

Resource type: ACADEMY_ORIGINAL_REFERENCE_WORK

REFERENCE WORK — Academy study for performance, presentation, and production craft. Purpose: give the learner a complete work, event map, process record, or described artifact to observe rather than inventing a missing source. Musical structure is the pattern of repetition, contrast, layering, and return that makes events relate across time. Reference content: An A–B–A plan can keep the pulse constant, change texture in B, and return to A more softly so the return is recognizable but not copied exactly. Supplied context: A repeated idea creates recognition; contrast changes expectation; return lets the listener compare what changed. Notation or an event map preserves those decisions for checking. Analysis boundary: first describe rhythm, contour, harmony, texture, form, dynamics, timbre, and phrase structure; then interpret; then use only the supplied context. Tradeoff available for evaluation: More layers can enrich texture but hide a main idea. More repetition can create coherence but become predictable without meaningful variation. Non-example of evidence use: Adding unrelated events without a preserved pattern makes the form difficult to hear or verify. This Academy instructional reference is not presented as an authentic historical or culturally specific work. Use it to study performance, presentation, and production craft; describe evidence before judging and adapt the demonstrated relationship rather than copying a finished work.

How to use it: Use the attached Academy-original reference work as the work under investigation; no outside artwork, recording, performance, or web source is required.

Rights: Manuel Academy original; licensed CC BY 4.0 for learner use and adaptation. No third-party text, image, score, lyric, melody, recording, or performance is included.

Access and materials: Household-accessible route: pencil or pen and scrap paper are enough. For sound or performance work, tap, clap, use spoken syllables, move a finger, or notate silently. Specialized art materials, instruments, paid software, cameras, microphones, and recording devices are optional and never affect credit.
critique_criteria: The submission contains the required work blocks and one reviewable process state; each required artifact, study, response, or process note can be located.
The learner locates relevant rhythm, contour, harmony, texture, form, dynamics, timbre, and phrase structure and explains how the evidence relates to the stated intent, claim, or criterion.
The learner states an intent or claim and supports it with observable evidence while retaining ownership of artistic decisions.
The process record shows a check and a learner-chosen revision or reasoned decision to keep the result.

presentation_and_privacy.presentation_options: You choose the audience. Keeping the work entirely to yourself, showing it to one parent or trusted adult, or submitting it as a file with no one watching are all full-credit options. No public performance, exhibition, class presentation, live audience, photograph, camera, or voice recording is required at any point in this task, and choosing the most private option never lowers the score.
presentation_and_privacy.text_or_no_audio_alternative: A written alternative is always available for spoken reflection, explanation, or critique and scores the same. Tap, point through, gesture, or use the supplied notation or event map without recording. A written or notated response can show structure and reasoning; it does not claim hearing or performed control that was not actually demonstrated. No instrument, microphone, camera, or public performance is required.

copyright_and_authorship: The graded submission must be your own authorship. A parent, tutor, or AI tool may explain an idea, demonstrate a technique, or give feedback on a draft, but must not produce, write, debug, or make any part of the work that is scored. Any material you did not create yourself must be in the public domain, openly licensed, or used as a short cited excerpt for study — reproduce no more than the point requires, credit the maker and the source, and never copy full lyrics, a complete score, or a whole image and present it as your own.
accessibility_options: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
For any multi-session project, supply a written milestone plan, checkpoint dates, and a task breakdown, so executive-function load is not silently part of what is being assessed.

Adjust quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode while holding the target constant. Where the target names a specific skill, change how it is evidenced rather than substituting a different skill.

Accept typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, notated, constructed, or demonstrated responses. Where performance is the target, a private demonstration to one trusted adult carries the same weight as any audience, and requires no recording.
Provide adaptive instruments and grips, enlarged or braille notation, seated and standing studio access, low-odour and low-dust material substitutes, and hearing protection on request.

Where documentation quality is itself the target, document the artwork alone with no person in frame, or have an adult verify the physical work directly. Neither route requires an image of the learner, and both preserve the documentation target rather than replacing it.
task_accessibility_provisions: Where performance is the target, a private demonstration to one trusted adult carries exactly the same weight as any audience, and requires no recording. A written or notated account of the intended performance is a full substitute.

Any model, source, or artifact under study is supplied in an accessible parallel form: text alternative or transcript, described version, and a tactile or enlarged rendering where the original is visual. The learner is never required to perceive the source in one specific channel to analyse it.
Breaks, extended time, a hidden timer, reduced copying, and a low-distraction setting are available on request and never reduce the score.
safety_and_privacy_rules: Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Protect hearing, ventilation, tool safety, cultural context, and respectful representation.
Public performance is never required. A private, low-audience, or written-and-scored alternative always carries the same academic target.
No recording of the learner’s voice, no photograph, and no video is ever required; documentation may be written, notated, sketched, or adult-verified instead.
Use only original, public-domain, licensed, or family-approved works. Do not reproduce full copyrighted lyrics, sheet music, or other protected works without documented rights.
The tutor may explain technique, ask diagnostic questions, and critique work, but never silently completes graded creative work.

media.fallback: Use the complete supplied beat map, script, evidence record, or event description. No teacher handout or outside search is required.

remediation: Route 1: Reduce performance, presentation, and production craft to three locatable events, areas, steps, or decisions. Label the intended effect beside each and underline the one rhythm relationship that should carry it. Use a separate small study, four-event loop, thumbnail, evidence table, or paper plan. The adult may model the noticing process on different material but may not change the learner’s work. Check yourself: Point to or name the exact rhythm evidence before deciding whether it serves the intent. New attempt: Put the support away and make a new arrangement, passage, response, or plan; record what the new evidence shows. Route 2: Return to the last understandable state. Hold every relationship steady except one chosen feature from rhythm, contour, harmony, texture, form, dynamics, timbre, and phrase structure; predict what that single change should do. Test the feature on scrap paper, a silent count, a two-event rehearsal loop, movable shapes, or a short evidence sentence before changing the scored work. Check yourself: Name what stayed the same, what changed, and the first observable result—without using “better” as the evidence. New attempt: Create a different small case using the same one-variable method, then transfer the finding to the original task only if it serves the learner’s intent.
extension: Apply performance, presentation, and production craft under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or explain the idea to someone else using an original example. Treat this as optional depth on performance, presentation, and production craft rather than extra volume: one harder case done well beats three more of the same. Extension work stays private by default and uses only original, public-domain, or properly cited material. Extension work is never required to reach mastery and must not be assigned as a penalty.
